properties.description:
TWO FINDINGS, and the split is the point.

`unverified_published_contract` names an Interface designated `published` or `both` that no PASSING check verifies. Per-contract, severity 0.6 — level with `unverified_enforced_rule` and above `unverified_capability`, on that finding's own reasoning: an unproven capability is work not yet confirmed, while this is an obligation to somebody ELSE that nobody can observe compliance with. Publishing is what raises it; an internal boundary with no check is not this finding. `both` is billed because it offers a contract as well as needing one; `required` is not, because a contract this design needs from OUTSIDE is somebody else's promise to prove.

`no_published_boundary` asks the posture question ONCE, aggregate, severity 0.3, when a design records boundaries and designates none of them published.

⭐ WHY THE SECOND ONE HAS TO EXIST, AND IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. `Interface.designation` DEFAULTS to `internal`, so a boundary nobody classified and one deliberately kept internal are stored identically — the schema says so in as many words, and `pair_designs` already refuses to paper over it. That makes a ZERO from the first detector genuinely ambiguous, and reporting it as clean would be the "a detector answering zero over an empty population reads exactly like one that ran clean" failure the loop refuses everywhere else. So the zero asks a question instead.
  Contrast `Artifact.audience`, which is deliberately UNDEFAULTED: silence there is legible as silence, so `internal_only_delivery` needs no such companion. The two detectors are siblings whose population reporting differs ONLY because one property has a default and the other does not — the clearest argument yet for `req:defaults-do-not-assert`.

🛑 IT COULD NOT HAVE EXISTED BEFORE 2026-08-21. `VERIFIES` could not reach an `Interface` at all until #291 (`fact:a-contract-is-the-one-thing-reflow2-cannot-attach-evidence-to`), so every contract in every design read as unverified and this would have fired on all of them — correctly and uselessly. The edge landed and exactly ONE check has been drawn since, on reflow2's own design: vocabulary with no detector, seen from outside. The finding's evidence SAYS SO, so a reader of an older design does not mistake the absence for neglect.

NARROW BY CONSTRUCTION: it fires only on what a design has already CHOSEN to publish, and a design with no boundaries at all is asked nothing — it has not declined to publish one, it has not got there, the same reasoning as `vocabulary_coverage`'s barely-started note.

MEASURED ON REFLOW2 ITSELF the day it was built: 3 published boundaries, 2 reported — `ifc:graph-export` and `ifc:mcp-tools-http`, both with zero incoming VERIFIES. `ifc:mcp-tools` is silent because it carries a passing check. Design-wide gaps 73 to 75.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-black-box-owes-an-interface-the-way-a-capability-owes-a-requirement`, which was read before this was created. That Decision is an OPEN brainstorm holding four options; this is the one that got built, and it is idea B in that node's own lettering. The relationship is the same as `cap:a-design-says-which-vocabulary-it-has-never-used` to its idea node: the Decision records what was considered, the Capability records what exists. Ideas A, C and D there remain open and unbuilt.

⚠️ NOT BUILT, AND DELIBERATELY: nothing here asks whether a published contract's SPEC is complete. `req:interface-spec-complete` is accepted and still unimplemented — 3 of 3 published boundaries here have 4 to 5 agreement fields unset. Adjacent, different work, and folding it in would have made one finding answer two questions.
properties.name: A published contract is asked for its evidence, and a design that publishes nothing is asked whether it meant to
